Riverside council approves new cycle lanes
Fairhaven Gazette, 21 October 2026
The Riverside district council voted 9 to 4 on Tuesday to build protected cycle lanes along Mill Road and Station Street, two of the busiest routes into the town centre.
The plan, which will cost EUR 2.4 million, removes about 60 parking spaces and adds raised kerbs, new crossings and a bus stop bypass. Work is due to start in March and finish by the end of 2027.

Supporters said the lanes would make the school run safer; collisions involving cyclists on Mill Road doubled between 2023 and 2025. Shop owners on Station Street argued that losing parking would hurt trade and asked for a loading bay, which the council agreed to add.
Councillor Ana Brightwater, who chairs the transport committee, said the council would publish traffic counts every six months so residents can judge the results.

Review: Aerobrew 300 coffee grinder
Rating: 2 out of 5 stars. Reviewed by a verified buyer, October 2026.
I wanted to like this grinder. It looks good on the counter and the hopper holds a full bag of beans.

The problems started in the first week. The grind is uneven on the fine settings, so espresso shots run fast and taste sour. The motor is loud enough to wake the house, and static makes the grounds stick to the chute.
After two months the timer dial stopped clicking into place. Customer service replied after nine days and offered a 10 percent coupon rather than a repair.
For the price there are quieter grinders with a more even grind. I would not buy it again.
The causes of the Dust Bowl
History 201 essay by Casey Linden, submitted 10 October 2026
The Dust Bowl was a time in the 1930s when big dust storms hit the American plains. There were many causes but the main ones were farming and drought.
Farmers plowed up a lot of grassland in the 1920s because wheat prices were high. The grass had held the soil in place. When the drought came, the soil dried out and the wind blew it away.
The drought lasted for most of the decade. Some years had almost no rain. Many families had to leave their farms and move west.
In conclusion, the Dust Bowl was caused by bad farming and drought together. The government later started programs to protect the soil.
